native_retrieval.title: Scoop: Trump's top MAGA advisers gather to plot midterms - Axios
native_retrieval.snippet: President Trump's top political advisers inside and outside of the White House are meeting Tuesday afternoon to review polling, their messaging and strategy ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms. * That doesn't include what insiders say is hundreds of millions of dollars more in Trump's dark-money political nonprofit, Securing American Greatness. **Zoom in:** The meeting at the Four Seasons hotel in D.C. is the second of what are becoming regular Trump team conclaves to coordinate the GOP, its candidates and his political operation. * Tony Fabrizio, Trump's longtime top pollster, who will give a presentation about the midterm picture. **Zoom out:** Republicans acknowledge it will be tough to maintain control of the U.S. House with Trump's poll numbers bottoming out amid rising gas prices and the war in Iran. * But Trump's political operatives say voters are wary of Democrats' progressive overreach, and they think this election will be about who Americans hate more, not who they love.

native_retrieval.title: Trump administration says it's deferring $1B in Medicaid payments to California and Minnesota - AP News
native_retrieval.snippet: Test Your News I.Q. 2026 Elections Election Results Election calendar White House Congress Supreme Court The latest AP-NORC polls. # Trump administration says it’s deferring $1B in Medicaid payments to California and Minnesota. The Trump administration on Tuesday said it was deferring more than $1 billion in Medicaid payments to Minnesota and California because of “suspected fraud and noncompliance,” the latest in a series of punitive steps it has linked to allegations of fraud in mostly Democratic-led states. Last month, California’s Medicaid director told a congressional committee that CMS had not yet provided “any instances of fraud, waste or abuse” to the state in its justification of a $1.3 billion Medicaid funding deferral announced in May. And in Minnesota, state officials have been executing a thorough corrective action plan to defray CMS concerns that have led the agency to defer some $260 million in federal money and to threaten future cuts.
